requirements.text: A page and its content are one simai.composition.document (schema_version 1) in JSON. The JSON Document is the canonical form and the only reversible exchange form; HTML, Markdown and Editor.js are conversions of it.
requirements.guidance: One standard, one document format, one version and one conformance kit (owner decision 2026-11-10). Canonical form and digest: normalize() in src/core/js/composition/index.mjs.

requirements.text: Types come in three sets. Layout is the set of the type registry; Content is the profile structured-content (the content.* types); Page is the profile ui-layout, which holds layout and content types together. The stored profile names stay ui-layout and structured-content in schema_version 1; a page profile named page waits for a schema_version 2.
requirements.guidance: Owner decision Q1 (2026-11-10): no migration; the reader name of ui-layout is the Page set.

requirements.text: A Document of a profile the reader does not know gives one diagnostic, profile_unknown, whatever its size; checks of a node against its profile run only for a known profile.

While a Document is edited, the model is the source of truth: a view never removes what it cannot draw, and a node it cannot edit stays where it is, held by its id. The editing operations and the behaviour of such nodes (islands) are not part of this edition.
requirements.guidance: They are fixed after the sf-input-rich prototype (assessment section 7, Q4 and Q5; assignment F3).

requirements.text: Inline content (inline model 1.2.0) is an array of entries: text runs with marks; links, which hold text runs and breaks; the break; and inline components from a closed list (badge, kbd, icon, button), never inside a link. Marks are a closed list (strong, em, code, strike) in any combination and a canonical order; a mark is never a style.

Normalising inline content merges equal neighbouring runs, sorts the known marks and keeps unknown ones after them, drops empty runs, joins neighbouring links of one address and splits a link around an inline component. The model never removes a break; the html@1 value projection applies the html@1 edge rule, which is idempotent.
requirements.guidance: inline-model.mjs normalizeInline; html-subset.mjs value mode (idempotent since 2026-11-10).

requirements.text: An unknown node, inline entry or mark survives every edit and every conversion: editing one part of a Document never changes another part, validation reports what it does not know, and a renderer draws nothing for it.
requirements.guidance: Assessment Q7; test plan items 2 and 2b.

requirements.text:
A break is a soft line break inside a block: {"type": "break", "marks"?: [...]}. HTML writes
; Markdown writes a backslash before the line end, and
in headings and table cells; an editor inserts one with Shift+Enter. A valid html@1 value converted to the model and back is the same bytes.
requirements.guidance: html-value.mjs: toHtml(fromHtml(v).value).value === v for every valid stored value v.

requirements.text: A block of another source the model cannot hold is content.foreign {source: markdown|editorjs|html, raw, hash}. raw is the exact source slice for markdown and html and the block value for editorjs; hash is sha256: of raw as UTF-8, written by normalize and every adapter. A public page draws nothing of it and an editor an inert placeholder; raw is never parsed into markup. It goes back only to its own source format, elsewhere in a reported carrier; a block whose hash does not match (foreign_hash_mismatch) is kept, not drawn and not written.
Every converter returns {value, losses: [{code, path, what}]}; nothing is lost silently. The guarantee table of this standard (extension simai.composition, conversions) is normative.

Markdown is a projection of structured content and of a single text area, not of a page: CommonMark with GFM tables and strike, and the Docara directives. Node ids are written only on directive blocks; elsewhere they belong to the source-preserving adapter's map. Layout has no standard Markdown form; a page is exchanged as JSON.

A Document uses the Framework's names (status, appearance, neutral, error). A format with names of its own is mapped by its adapter, and what the other side requires and the Document lacks is reported, not invented.
requirements.guidance: Docara alert: type <-> status, variant <-> appearance, clear <-> neutral, danger <-> error, the first heading <-> data.title; a title-less alert is docara_alert_title_required.

requirements.text: props are the parameters a type declares; presentation is a view, a preset and modifiers from registered lists, printed as utility classes. No style and no class name stands anywhere in a Document.
requirements.guidance: style is a forbidden key since 2026-11-10 (kit 2.0.0).

requirements.text: A Document carries schema_version; every type manifest carries its version. A minor version only adds; a breaking change is a new type name or a new schema_version.
A producer writes a new inline entry or type only to hosts whose Framework pair knows it; an older editor keeps it opaque and an older validator refuses it.

Publishing fails closed: by default a renderer refuses a Document it cannot fully validate and draws nothing, so a host keeps its last valid version; a placeholder for what it does not know is for an editor's canvas only.

A renderer of structured content passes the conformance kit (contracts/conformance/structured-content), its cases and its converter fixtures; a second renderer, in another language, passes the same kit.
requirements.guidance: Kit 2.1.0 is pinned by this edition.

uses.description: The Recipe contract: a page's layout, its regions and their inherit, replace and clear. Unchanged by this standard.
The type manifest: a type's version, profiles, slots, data and props schemas, and presentation.
The conformance kit of structured content: its manifest names every case and converter fixture and the type versions it was written for.

references.description: How a consumer reads which Framework pair carries this edition.

simai.ownership.scope_note: The editing architecture (operations, history, islands, block clipboard) is not in 1.0.0; it follows the sf-input-rich prototype and the owner's yes.

conversions.guarantee: lossless for html@1; anything else cleaned away and reported
toHtml(fromHtml(v)) === v for every valid value
conversions.unknown: marks code and strike, inline components, other types: not_expressible

conversions.guarantee: content set and single text areas; lossless but for node ids of blocks without a directive, presentation, bindings, extensions, figure size, table header column/both/none and caption; a block the model cannot hold is content.foreign with its source text

SIMAI -> Editor.js -> SIMAI equal including ids (sf-<type> tools); Editor.js -> SIMAI -> Editor.js the same value for the standard tools and foreign blocks; inline HTML outside the mapped tags reported
